title: kv-cache: defrag-aware eviction, adaptive paging & spillover prioritization
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Improves KV cache memory management: introduces defragmentation pass, adaptive paging thresholds, and spillover prioritization to reduce OOMs and tail latency. No API changes.
description:
Context & motivation: Memory fragmentation in the KV cache was causing unpredictable OOMs and latency spikes for long-running chat sessions and high-concurrency workloads. Previous heuristics only evicted by last-access time which led to poor compaction on fragmented GPU allocations and aggressive paging to host memory. This PR adds a defrag-aware eviction policy, an adaptive paging threshold, and a spillover prioritizer so the runtime can make eviction decisions that reduce fragmentation and avoid unnecessary host-device page thrashing.

What this PR does (summary):
- Implement a compacting/defragmentation pass in the KV cache manager that coalesces adjacent cold KV entries during low-util periods. The pass is bounded and incremental to avoid impacting latency SLOs.
- Add an eviction priority group model: hot / warm / cold groups are computed from access recency, token-span, and batch hit-rate. Evictions prefer cold fragments that reduce fragmentation ratio.
- Adaptive paging thresholds: the runtime dynamically raises/lower device->host paging thresholds based on free device pages, recent page-fault rate, and active batch sizes.
- Spillover prioritizer: when spilling to host or remote storage, the manager tags entries with compressibility and rehydration cost so we prefer spilling entries that are cheap to restore.
- Scheduling & kernel hints: expose lightweight kernel-scheduling hints from the KV layer so the serving runtime can schedule defrag/evict work during natural batching gaps and uses lower-priority CUDA streams to reduce interference with generation.
- Continuous batching integration: ensure batching logic avoids thrashing by skipping immediate re-fetches for recently-evicted prefixes within a grace window.
- Tests & benchmarks: unit tests for eviction correctness, integration tests for paging/spillover paths, and perf bench showing improvements on representative workloads.

Commits (high-level):
- a1b2c3d: refactor kv_cache manager public API to expose occupancy metrics
- b2c3d4e: add adaptive paging controller and heuristics
- c3d4e5f: implement incremental defrag pass and compaction bookkeeping
- d4e5f6a: spillover prioritizer and compressibility tagging
- e5f6a7b: kernel scheduling hints + integration with scheduler
- f6a7b8c: tests, benchmarks, and CI perf assertions

Files changed (high-level):
- runtime/kv_cache/manager.cpp (new defrag loop, occupancy APIs)
- runtime/kv_cache/manager.h
- runtime/kv_cache/defrag.cpp / defrag.h (incremental compaction implementation)
- runtime/kv_cache/eviction_policy.cpp (priority groups + heuristics)
- runtime/scheduler/scheduler.cpp (accept scheduler hints, low-priority streams)
- serving/batching/batcher.cpp (grace window logic to avoid cache thrash)
- perf/bench/kv_cache_bench.cc (new microbench harness)
- tests/kv_cache_eviction_test.cpp, tests/paging_integration_test.cpp
- ci/perf-check.yaml (add perf CI gating)

Benchmarks & results:
- Synthetic chat workload (50 concurrent sessions, 32-token average prefix): 18% increase in steady-state token throughput, 30% reduction in OOMs seen in long-run (24h) soak tests, 25% fewer device->host page faults under mix workload.
- Tail latency (p95 for response generation) improved by ~12% under high load due to less paging during critical paths.

Backward compatibility & safety: No external API changes. Defrag pass is opt-in behind feature flag "kv.defrag_enabled" and defaults to true for upcoming release. Parameters are tunable via runtime config; conservative defaults chosen to avoid latency regressions.

Review conversation (high-level):
- Evan Li (reviewer): "Nice work — defrag looks promising. A few questions: how do we bound CPU/GPU work for the compaction pass? Can we avoid lock contention on the main read path?"
- Author (Asha): "Defrag is incremental and only operates on cold slabs; we added a per-shard budget and yield points. Reads acquire lock-free read path; compaction uses a lightweight write lock per-shard and signals backpressure to scheduler via hints."
- Maya Thompson (reviewer): "Can paging thresholds oscillate? We should add smoothing to avoid flip-flopping. Also add metrics for fragments/compactions performed."
- Author: "Added exponential smoothing to the paging controller and exported two new metrics: kv_cache_fragmentation_ratio and kv_defrag_runs_total."
- Ravi Menon (approver): "LGTM after one nit on test coverage for multi-GPU bleeding edge. Confirmed perf numbers locally."

CI summary: build: pass; unit-tests: pass; integration-tests (paging): pass after one rerun; lint: pass; perf-check: initially failed (regression due to aggressive default), reverted aggressive default and re-ran perf-check: pass. All checks green on merge.

Deployment & rollout plan:
- Feature gated (kv.defrag_enabled) so we can enable per-cluster. Start with Dedicated staging pools for 1 week, monitor kv_cache_fragmentation_ratio, device_page_fault_rate, defrag_run_time_ms, and error rates. Gradual rollout to hosted pools with canary and automatic rollback if device OOM rate increases.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main on 2026-02-19 after approvals by Evan and Ravi and successful CI.

Notes for on-call/SRE: If enabling in production observe the new metrics and set alerts: kv_cache_fragmentation_ratio>0.35 for >10m, device_page_fault_rate spike >3x baseline, kv_defrag_run_time_ms >500ms. Revert flag or reduce defrag budget if latency regressions are observed.

Related work: builds on previous PRs for spillover heuristics and defrag prototypes (see PRs 99512 and 101235), aligns with ENG-8421 roadmap item for robust memory management.
